cards.text: This is a Shiggaion that David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), sang to the LORD about the words of Cush, a Benjamite. The psalm never says what Cush said, and I am NOT about to make it up. David opens by taking refuge in the LORD and asking Him to save him from all his pursuers.

cards.question: David says his pursuers will shred his soul like a lion. What else does he say they'll do to him?
David says his pursuers will tear him to pieces. True or false: he says someone else will be there to rescue him.

cards.text: Then David puts himself on trial: if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands. That's like telling your boss, "Go ahead, PULL the security footage," and you only say that when you KNOW what's on the tape.

cards.question: David keeps going with his if-I-did-it list. True or false: one item on it is rewarding his ally with evil.
David says that if he really has done these things, what should happen to him?

answers.text: Let his enemy trample him down
Let the LORD forgive him anyway
Let the elders settle the matter

cards.text: Then David's if-I-did-it list is done, and he calls out: "Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies." No whispering in this prayer, friend, because this is the LOUD part.

cards.question: With his enemies in a fury, David cries, "Awake, my God," and asks Him to do what?

cards.text: Now David paints a HUGE picture: the assembled peoples gathered around the LORD, and the LORD taking His seat over them on high. It's like when the whole company gets called into one room, and the big boss takes the chair up front.

cards.question: With the peoples gathered around Him, David says the LORD ___ the peoples.
David asks the LORD to vindicate him. True or false: he asks for it according to his royal rank.

cards.text: David asks God to put an end to the evil of the wicked and establish the righteous. Down here, somebody can send a thumbs-up in the group chat while they're FUMING on the other end of that phone, but that doesn't work with this Judge.

cards.question: What does David say the righteous God searches?

cards.text: Next, David tells us where his protection is. Friend, when the pressure is on, you find out FAST who's really got your back.

cards.question: David says his shield is with ___, who saves the upright in heart.
David calls God a righteous judge. True or false: David says God feels indignation only once in a while.

cards.text: Then the picture turns sharp, and it starts with an if: if it holds, God will sharpen His sword, and His bow, His deadly weapons and His fiery arrows are already prepared. Me, I've got an oven timer, and that's my WHOLE arsenal.

cards.question: David says God will sharpen His sword. When?

cards.text: Now David turns the spotlight on the wicked man, and he uses a picture of pregnancy: the man travails with evil and conceives trouble. That one's been on the way for a WHILE, friend, and nobody is throwing it a shower.

cards.question: In David's picture, the wicked man conceives trouble. What happens to it?

cards.text: The wicked man digs a hole and hollows it out. I bet he even stepped back to admire it.

cards.question: True or false: the wicked man ends up falling into the hole he dug.

cards.text: His trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head. Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in a junk drawer I didn't even build, and this man DUG his!
After the swords, the arrows and the pit, David turns back to the LORD. He says he will "sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High."

cards.question: David also says he will thank the LORD for His ___.
